short_definition: Software that continuously monitors endpoint devices to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats.
layman_explanation: A security guard dog stationed directly at every computer desk, watching for suspicious activity.

short_definition: Integrating security telemetry across endpoints, networks, cloud, and email for unified threat visibility.
layman_explanation: Connecting security guards at desks, cameras in hallways, and alarms at gates into one master control team.

short_definition: Software designed to detect, prevent, and remove malicious software from individual computers.
layman_explanation: A digital guard scanning downloaded files against a list of known malicious signatures.

short_definition: Advanced endpoint protection using artificial intelligence and behavioral analytics rather than simple signatures.
layman_explanation: A security guard that identifies bad behavior rather than just looking at mugshots.

short_definition: Acquiring, testing, and installing software updates to fix security vulnerabilities on endpoints.
layman_explanation: Regularly repairing broken window latches and door locks in your home to keep burglars out.

short_definition: Software allowing IT administrators to monitor, manage, and secure employee mobile devices remotely.
layman_explanation: A remote control panel allowing companies to wipe or lock work phones if they are lost.

short_definition: Securing a computer system by reducing its attack surface and disabling unneeded services.
layman_explanation: Boarding up unused basement windows and installing heavy locks on every door.

short_definition: A firewall application installed directly on a single computer host to filter its inbound and outbound traffic.
layman_explanation: An individual security guard stationed specifically at your bedroom door.

short_definition: Encrypting an entire computer storage drive to protect data at rest if the physical device is stolen.
layman_explanation: Locking your entire hard drive inside a safe so no one can read files if your laptop is stolen.

short_definition: Built-in full disk encryption features provided by Windows and macOS operating systems.
layman_explanation: The factory-installed deadbolt lock that secures your laptop's storage drive automatically.

short_definition: A dedicated hardware microchip designed to secure hardware through integrated cryptographic keys.
layman_explanation: A tamper-proof vault chip inside your laptop motherboard holding your master cryptographic keys.

short_definition: Security policies restricting or blocking external storage devices from connecting to endpoints.
layman_explanation: Gluing physical lock caps onto USB ports so employees cannot plug in unauthorized flash drives.

short_definition: An endpoint policy permitting only pre-approved applications to execute, blocking all others.
layman_explanation: A club bouncer letting you in only if your exact name is written on the guest list.

short_definition: A policy preventing specific known harmful or unauthorized programs from running on a device.
layman_explanation: Posting a list of known troublemakers at the door so security rejects them automatically.

short_definition: A security standard ensuring a device boots using only software trusted by the Original Equipment Manufacturer.
layman_explanation: Checking that the ignition key is authentic before allowing a car engine to start.

short_definition: Software monitoring local endpoints to prevent unauthorized copying or transmission of sensitive files.
layman_explanation: A guard preventing workers from printing or copying confidential documents onto personal USB drives.

short_definition: Mechanisms designed to stop attacks targeting newly discovered vulnerabilities before patches exist.
layman_explanation: Wearing a bulletproof vest that protects against new weapon types that haven't been cataloged yet.

short_definition: Monitoring system activities for abnormal patterns rather than checking static file signatures.
layman_explanation: Watching if a visitor acts suspiciously, like trying every door handle, rather than checking their face.

short_definition: A feature using virtualization-based security to isolate domain credentials from operating system memory.
layman_explanation: Storing admin master passwords inside a separate locked box that even the main operating system cannot directly read.

short_definition: A security technique randomizing system memory locations to prevent buffer overflow exploits.
layman_explanation: Randomly rearranging room numbers in a hotel daily so intruders cannot locate specific offices.

short_definition: A system feature marking memory regions as non-executable to block code execution from data spaces.
layman_explanation: Marking storage bins as 'read-only' so the computer refuses to run executable code placed inside them.

short_definition: Using hardware virtualization to create a secure isolated memory region away from the main OS.
layman_explanation: Creating a separate, miniature computer inside your computer to handle high-security tasks.

short_definition: Exploiting system bugs to elevate a standard user account to local administrator or SYSTEM permissions.
layman_explanation: A hotel guest finding a trick to swap their room key for the manager's master keycard.

short_definition: A capability allowing administrators to erase all data on a lost or stolen endpoint device remotely.
layman_explanation: Pressing a panic button from afar that disintegrates all documents inside a lost briefcase.

short_definition: An installed software package that analyzes local system behavior and blocks unauthorized actions.
layman_explanation: A bodyguard walking beside you who intercepts anyone trying to grab your bag.

short_definition: Examining operating system and application files to detect unauthorized changes or tampering.
layman_explanation: Checking the wax seals on official records daily to make sure no one modified them overnight.

short_definition: A Windows process responsible for enforcing security policy and handling user logins.
layman_explanation: The security officer inside Windows who checks your password and hands out access tokens.

short_definition: An attack technique extracting plaintext passwords or hashes directly from LSASS process memory.
layman_explanation: Pickpocketing the security officer's wallet while he is working to steal master keys.

short_definition: Data collected from endpoints—such as process starts, network connections, and file edits—for security monitoring.
layman_explanation: The activity log recording every single door opened, key turned, and file moved on a computer.

short_definition: Security policies governing personal employee devices used to access corporate data.
layman_explanation: Rules specifying how employees must secure their personal cars if they use them for business deliveries.

short_definition: Isolating corporate applications and data into a secure encrypted enclave on personal mobile devices.
layman_explanation: Placing a company-owned safe inside an employee's personal bedroom.

short_definition: Configurable settings that prevent common malware attack vectors, such as blocking Word macros from launching child processes.
layman_explanation: Setting strict rules like 'Documents are never allowed to launch executable programs.'

short_definition: Disconnecting a compromised device from the network remotely while maintaining an EDR management channel.
layman_explanation: Quarantining an infected person in a sealed room while keeping an intercom line open.

short_definition: Identifying unauthorized or unmanaged devices connected to an enterprise network.
layman_explanation: Scanning a parking lot to spot cars that don't display an official employee parking sticker.

short_definition: Checking a device's compliance status (e.g., active OS patches and firewall) before allowing network access.
layman_explanation: Inspecting a vehicle's brakes and tires before letting it onto a racetrack.

short_definition: A Windows security feature asking permission before allowing applications to make administrative changes.
layman_explanation: A pop-up prompt asking 'Are you sure you want to let this program make changes to your computer?'

short_definition: Configuring local endpoint firewalls to block unauthorized software from connecting out to the internet.
layman_explanation: Blocking unauthorized programs on your computer from making outgoing phone calls.

short_definition: Storing endpoint disk encryption recovery keys centrally in active directory for emergency access.
layman_explanation: Keeping a spare master key to every company laptop in a safe at corporate headquarters.

short_definition: A Windows interface allowing applications to integrate with the installed antimalware product to inspect script memory.
layman_explanation: A bridge allowing Windows PowerShell to ask Antivirus software 'Is this script safe to run?'

short_definition: An evasion technique where an attacker replaces the executable code of a legitimate process with malicious code.
layman_explanation: Emptying out a legitimate delivery van and putting a team of burglars inside while keeping the outside logo intact.

short_definition: Forcing a running program to load an external Dynamic Link Library containing malicious code.
layman_explanation: Slipping a fake instruction page into an actor's script binder right before they go on stage.

short_definition: Exploiting Windows search order paths to trick legitimate applications into loading malicious DLLs.
layman_explanation: Placing a fake tool in a hallway so a worker picks it up instead of walking to the real tool shed.

short_definition: Placing fake credentials and files on endpoints to trap and detect attackers moving laterally.
layman_explanation: Leaving a fake password document on your desktop titled 'Master Passwords' that triggers an alarm when opened.

short_definition: Securing the low-level firmware that initializes device hardware before the operating system loads.
layman_explanation: Locking the underlying engine compartment of a car so no one can tamper with the starter motor.

short_definition: Creating tamper-proof backups of local endpoint data that cannot be altered or deleted by ransomware.
layman_explanation: Writing your important documents onto read-only optical discs that cannot be overwritten.

short_definition: A Windows feature creating backup snapshots of computer files or volumes automatically.
layman_explanation: Taking automatic background photos of your computer files so you can restore old versions if needed.

short_definition: A Windows system service that logs detailed system activity to the event log for security analysis.
layman_explanation: A high-definition security camera logging every single process change and file creation on your PC.

short_definition: Treating all endpoints as potentially compromised regardless of whether they are on the local network.
layman_explanation: Assuming every laptop in the office might be infected, so every request requires fresh verification.
